title: Stare, Then Look Away: The Science of Afterimages
summary:
Here is a trick you can try. Stare at a brightly colored picture for 30 to 60 seconds, then look at a plain white surface. You will see a ghostly copy of the picture, the same shape and size, but in different colors. This is called an afterimage. A science experiment from Science Buddies explains why it happens.

Your eyes see color using special cells called cone cells. They sit in a tiny spot at the back of the eye called the fovea, which is only about 1 square millimeter in size. There are three types of cone cells, loosely called red, green and blue, based on the kind of light they respond to best. When you look at something red, your red cones send a message to your brain that says the object is red.

When red, green and blue light are added together, they make white light. So when you look at something white, all three types of cones are working at once.

But cone cells can get tired. If you stare at a red circle for a long time, your red cones become fatigued and stop responding for a moment. Then, when you look at a white surface, only your green and blue cones send messages to your brain. So you see a blue-green circle instead.

After several seconds, the red cones recover and the afterimage fades away.

You can even predict an afterimage's color. It is the complementary color of the original object. Complementary colors are two colors of light that make white when combined, such as red and cyan, green and magenta, or blue and yellow. The project invites you to test different colors and see how your own cone cells respond.
why_it_matters: The experiment shows that what we see depends on how our eye cells and brain work together, not just on the object itself. It is an easy way to explore human biology at home.

background_read: Light enters the eye and lands on the retina at the back, where special cells turn it into signals for the brain.
Cone cells handle color, and each of the three types responds best to red, green or blue light.
When red, green and blue light are mixed together, they make white light, which is different from mixing paints.
Cells that work hard for a long time can become tired, and this is what creates the ghostly colors of an afterimage.
